text:
Priya S.: Heads up — planning sync for Black Friday surge. Need a quick call on GPU mesh routing + fairness so we don't hit regional tails. Thinking of enabling 'mesh smoothing' for 8h windows around peak.
Dan M.: +1. Do we have projections for peak qps per region? I want to validate backlog and KV cache hit assumptions.
Alex K.: Latest sim: EU peak qps ~210k, NA peak ~480k, APAC ~95k. GPU-hour burn estimate with current binpacking is 164k hours/day at peak. (from synthetic-run-1917)
Ruth L.: That binpack number assumes no cross-region routing. If we allow mesh spillover to NA from EU during NA off-peak we cut peak GPU-hours by ~12% in sim.
jen_prod: Can we tolerate cross-region routing for EU customers? Data residency concerns were flagged by security for some enterprise tenants.
Priya S.: We'll exclude enterprise_tier=residency_required from cross-region spill. Default traffic can be floated. Need policy draft for routing decisions.
Dan M.: Proposal sketch (very small):
```json
{
  "policy": "mesh-smoothing-v1",
  "spill_threshold": 0.85,
  "max_cross_region_ratio": 0.12,
  "protected_tags": ["residency_required","gdpr_sensitive"]
}
```
Alex K.: Implementation notes: runtime can do prefix-aware KV replication for spill cases but adds ~8-12ms p50. We should only activate when tail risk of queued requests > 300ms.
Ruth L.: Also watch network egress cost — cross-region hops will add ~$0.02 per 1M tokens for APAC<->NA in our pricing model. For the projected traffic that becomes material (~$6k/day) unless we cap spill.
Priya S.: Tradeoff: extra $6k/day vs saving ~20k GPU-hours/day (est). That's about ~$0.3M/day saving if GPU-hour price is $15/hr? Wait that math seems off — re-evaluate.
Dan M.: Quick calc: 20k GPU-hours * $3.75/hr (committed pool blended avg) = $75k/day saved. So even with egress we're net positive.
jen_prod: Can we do a canary: enable mesh-smoothing only for non-enterprise traffic in lower-traffic AZs first, and monitor latency and errors for 2h windows? If green, expand.
Alex K.: Dev plan: flagging at routing layer + config flip. Need a migration window; suggest Thu 03:00-05:00 UTC for initial canary. Will also pre-warm KV caches to reduce coldstart.
Ruth L.: Ops checklist:
- pre-warm caches in target spill recipients
- raise alert thresholds for cross-region tail errors
- set automatic rollback if p99 latency increases > 15%
- monitor egress cost burn with hourly sampling
infra-bot: [metric snapshot] 1918001234: current cluster util p95=0.67, p99=0.89, avg qps=312k, coldstart_rate=0.021
Priya S.: OK let's lock Thu 03:00-05:00 UTC for canary. Dan/Alex do infra changes, Ruth will own rollout ops and alerting, jen_prod will coordinate product comms with enterprise PMs.
Dan M.: I'll file infra PR and link to this thread. PR will include config and simulation results.
Alex K.: I'll add a brief runbook section for rollback commands. Example rollback:
```bash
# switch off mesh smoothing
curl -X POST $CONTROLPLANE/api/v1/route-config -d '{"mesh":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI"
```
Ruth L.: Noted. Also I'll add a throttling policy in case we see token spikes: cap per-customer token rate to 200k tokens/min during canary window.
jen_prod: I'll draft the customer-facing note for enterprise teams and confirm the protected tags list.
Priya S.: Thanks team. Post-canary we'll compare GPU-hour burn and tail latency and decide on permanent default. If anyone finds issues before Thu, ping here.
Alex K.: tagging @infra-bot to kick a dry-run tomorrow morning 09:00 UTC.
infra-bot: scheduled dry-run: 1918001400, will run synthetic traffic with mesh-smoothing enabled for 30m and emit report.
Priya S.: Perfect. End of thread.
